title: A Veil for the Thorn Again
premise: Hazel Dunmore, a hedge-witch hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-forbidden city of Corvale, inherits a dying stranger's map to the Thorn Gate—the sealed door he has secretly kept shut for five years. The map reveals that King Aldric is no longer human: something called the Veilwraith wears his crown and feeds on the city's outlawed magic, growing stronger each season. Pursued by the king's witch-hunters and betrayed by allies on both sides, Hazel must reopen the gate he swore never to touch, journey into the thorned otherworld beyond it, and sever the wraith's bond before the winter solstice. In the end Hazel defeats the Veilwraith by offering it truth instead of power, frees the broken king, and chooses to stand openly as Corvale's gatekeeper—no longer invisible, but belonging at last.
about_author: Hazel Pemberton is a former archivist who left academia to write fantasy rooted in folklore and quiet rebellion. She lives near the coast, where she collects maps of places that do not exist.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Hazel Dunmore's POV. We meet Hazel selling harmless charms in Corvale, where magic is outlawed, and glimpse his nightly ritual checking the hidden Thorn Gate beneath his shop. When a bleeding stranger stumbles in murmuring about 'the crown,' Hazel's careful invisibility begins to crack. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Map Pressed into Unwilling Hands
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The stranger dies in Hazel's back room, pressing a bloodstained map into his hands and whispering that the king is already gone. Witch-hunters raid the street hours later, and Hazel realizes the map marks not just the gate—but the throne room itself. Emotional beat: fear hardening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Sera Vane, a witch-hunter who suspects the king's decrees have grown inhumanly cruel. Watching the monarch at court, she notices he casts no shadow at certain angles. Her doubt plants the novel's loyalty-versus-truth thread. Emotional beat: unease disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Old Debt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel seeks out Bramble, an exiled fae-tinkerer who once helped him seal the gate, and learns the map belongs to a dead order of gatekeepers. Bramble refuses to help unless Hazel admits why he really fled the otherworld five years ago. Emotional beat: shame surfacing.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Register
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera is ordered to burn a suspected charm-house; inside she finds children's toys charmed for good dreams, not weapons. She falsifies her report for the first time, and her commander watches her do it. Emotional beat: complicity taking root.

chapters.title: The Road Through Thornfield
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Bramble leave the city along the map's route, pursued by hunters. Crossing Thornfield moor, they are ambushed by thorn-wights—creatures that should have stayed beyond the gate—and Hazel barely repels them with magic he swore off using. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: An Audience of Shadows
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Summoned before the king alone, Sera is tested by questions only the true Aldric could answer—and the thing on the throne answers wrong. It lets her live, which frightens her more than death would. Emotional beat: terror wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: The Inn at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At a border inn, Hazel meets Odile, a charming scholar who offers safe passage—and whom Bramble privately warns is a spy for the crown. Torn between loneliness and caution, Hazel half-trusts her. Emotional beat: longing for connection versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Odile sells their location to the hunters; Sera leads the ambush but hesitates when she sees Hazel protect a child during the fighting. Bramble is captured; Hazel escapes with the map torn in half. Emotional beat: guilt and fury intertwined.

chapters.title: The Half-Truth of Maps
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Interrogating Bramble, Sera learns the Veilwraith's name and its hunger for bound oaths. Bramble argues that she serves the very thing she hunts. That night she burns her commission seal. Emotional beat: loyalty breaking against truth.

chapters.title: Below the City of Bells
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel slips back into Corvale through forgotten catacombs to find the gate's twin key, guided by rumors of a smuggler-priest who remembers the old rites. He discovers the city's foundations are themselves grown from living thorn. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Forgot His God
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The smuggler-priest, Father Ilex, agrees to forge the key but demands Hazel confess his secret: five years ago Hazel fled the otherworld rather than face the guardian there, leaving his sister behind. The confession costs him everything he pretends to be. Emotional beat: grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Winter Court
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the solstice eve feast, the Veilwraith announces a purge of all 'tainted' citizens. Sera sees the king's true face flicker beneath the mask—one moment of the real Aldric screaming silently for help. Emotional beat: compassion overriding fear.

chapters.title: Two Halves Make a Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Sera defects, bringing Bramble's freedom and her knowledge of the palace wards. Mending the torn map, Hazel learns the gate opens only for one who carries both worlds' blood—and that the Veilwraith wants him to open it. Emotional beat: wary alliance, dawning trap.

chapters.title: The Price of Keys
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Father Ilex completes the key but dies holding the ward against hunters, buying them the night. Hazel, Sera, and Bramble descend to the Thorn Gate as the solstice moon rises. Emotional beat: sacrifice transforming resolve into purpose.

chapters.title: Beyond the Veil
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They cross into the thorned otherworld, where Hazel confronts the guardian he abandoned—revealed as his sister, transformed by her long watch. She grants passage only if he accepts what he owes. Emotional beat: reckoning and forgiveness entangled.

chapters.title: The Root of the Crown
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. In the wraith's root-lair beneath both worlds, Bramble uncovers its origin: a king's oath made in desperation, corrupted over centuries. Power was never stolen—it was invited. Emotional beat: tragic understanding of corruption's mechanics.

chapters.title: Storming the Glass Palace
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. While Sera turns the palace guard with proof of the king's shadowless face, Hazel fights through thorn-grown corridors toward the throne. Bramble falls covering their retreat, alive but bound in thorns. Emotional beat: courage sharpened by loss.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the King
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Confronting the Veilwraith, Hazel is offered everything he ever wanted—belonging, power, his sister restored—if he kneels and reopens the gate fully. He nearly does. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Truth Instead of Power
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax. Instead of fighting, Hazel speaks the wraith's own origin back to it—the lonely oath, the fear that made it—unbinding the lie that sustains it. The wraith unravels; the true king collapses free. Emotional beat: triumph through honesty, not force.

chapters.title: A Crown Set Down
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The freed Aldric abdicates, naming a council that includes voices from both worlds; Sera is asked to lead the new order of gatekeepers. The purge is reversed, and magic is neither outlawed nor worshipped but governed. Emotional beat: weary hope.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Epilogue. Hazel reopens the Thorn Gate—not to flee, but as a living bridge tended openly, his sister crossing freely at last. Hanging his charm-shop sign beside a new one reading GATEKEEPER, he finally belongs to both worlds. Emotional beat: homecoming and peace.
